newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares retreat as coalition hopes melt.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares retreat as coalition hopes melt.

text.p: Turkish shares retreated five percent from record highs on Tuesday as hopes of a secularist coalition began to melt away in the face of division among right-wing parties.
Brokers said the failure of two rival conservative parties to agree on forming an anti-Islamist alliance ate away steadily at eight percent gains on Monday.
The IMKB National-100 index sank 5.07 percent, or 90 points, to end the day at 1,684. Trading volume slipped to 34.4 trillion lira ($235 million) from 45.5 trillion on Monday.
"The market was irritated by the possibility that the conservative True Path Party may not support the new alliance," said Okan Gulek from Taksim Securities.

True Path leader Tansu Ciller, allied with the Islamists of outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan, met her rival Mesut Yilmaz on Tuesday and rejected his alliance offer. Her comments added force to an earlier party vote against a Yilmaz coalition.
"Until a government is formed and there is a confidence vote I think we will continue to see these ups and downs," said Ilhami Koc of Is Investment.
Utility Cukurova Elektrik and flat steel maker Eregli led share activity, brokers said.
The heavy wave of selling was exacerbated by the comments of leftist leader Deniz Baykal, who agreed to support a Yilmaz-led coalition but told supporters he sought elections by the end of the year.
"Baykal's remarks also had a negative effect," Gulek said.
Yilmaz has said he does not want to take the country to polls before next spring. He was asked last week to replace Erbakan who stepped down after months of army criticism.
Yilmaz is short of the simple parliament majority needed to win a confidence vote even with the support of two left-wing parties and a right-wing group which broke away from the DYP.

Optimism about the prospects of a secularist coalition underpinned the market. But shares were expected to remain vulnerable to any negative signals emerging from talks between political leaders, brokers said.

"Our expectations for political developments are reasonably positive. But if an agreement cannot be reached then uncertainty could once more take control of the market," said Toprak Securities broker Vedat Konyyali.
The Turkish lira eased to 146,460 to the dollar, compared with the central bank's key dollar rate of 146,200 on Monday.
Bond yields edged higher after sharp declines to around 100 percent on Monday from 105 percent. The most active bond's yield rose slightly to 100.66 pct from 100.55 pct.
